chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Al-Hasan ibn Al-Jahm, from Zareeh, who said:
I heard Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) saying: 'When the juice simmers or boils, it is Prohibited'.
ai.seo_question: When does grape juice become haram according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) links the prohibition of grape juice to the physical signs of fermentation, specifically when it 'simmers' or 'boils,' marking the transition from fresh juice to an intoxicating state. This ruling reflects the Shia jurisprudential principle that the threshold for *khamr* (intoxicant) is determined by the onset of fermentation, ensuring that beverages remain permissible until they acquire the potential to intoxicate. The emphasis on sensory indicators like boiling highlights the practical application of *nushrah* (fermentation) in distinguishing between *asir* and *khamr*.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal Bin Al Jahm, from Zareeh who said,
‘I heard Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘When the (grape) juice simmer or boils, it is Prohibited’.
en.sarwar: 4. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ibn Faddal from al-Hassan ibn al-Jahm from Dharih who has said the following: “
I once heard abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, saying, ‘When juice (grape juice) begins to simmer or boil it becomes unlawful to use it for drink.’”
